348575.title: q-gamma positivity conjecture for alternating Eulerian polynomials
348575.literal_statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)$ denote the alternating descent number and alternating major index of $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$. Define the bivariate alternating Eulerian polynomial by 
$$
\widehat{A}_n(t,q)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n}t^{\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)}q^{\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)}.
$$
 **q-gamma positivity conjecture.** The polynomial $\widehat{A}_n(t,q)$ has the expansion 
$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n}t^{\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)}q^{\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)}=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)q^{\binom{k+1}{2}}(-t)^k\prod_{i=k+1}^{n-1-k}(1+tq^i),
$$
 where $\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)\in\mathbb{N}[q]$ and $(1+q)^k$ divides $\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)$. This is presented as an alternating analogue of the known $q$-$\gamma$-positivity expansion for Eulerian--Mahonian polynomials; the claimed coefficient positivity and divisibility are not established in the supplied text.

348961.title: Coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture for the four-parameter recurrence triangle
348961.literal_statement:
Let $a,c,d,e$ be algebraic indeterminates, and define $T(n,k)$ by

$$
T(n,k)=[a(n-k)+c]T(n-1,k-1)+(dk+e)T(n-1,k)
$$

for $n\geq 1$, with $T(0,k)=\delta_{k0}$. Thus $\bm{T}=(T(n,k))_{n,k\geq 0}$ is a lower-triangular matrix over $\mathbb{Z}[a,c,d,e]$. A polynomial is nonnegative in the coefficientwise order when all its coefficients are nonnegative, and a polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all its minors have nonnegative coefficients. **Four-parameter coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture.** The lower-triangular matrix $\bm{T}$ defined by the recurrence above is coefficientwise totally positive in the indeterminates $a,c,d,e$. This conjecture would imply the clean Eulerian and reversed Stirling conjectures under the specializations $(a,c,d,e)=(1,1,1,1)$ and $(1,0,0,1)$, respectively; the source gives no proof of the general assertion.

381554.title: Infinitesimal rigidity of hinged spanning cycles on the hypercube
381554.literal_statement: Let the $n$-Roberts graph encode the facet adjacencies of the $n$-cube, and let a **hinged spanning cycle** be a spanning cycle of this graph whose corresponding $2n$ facet adjacencies are retained as hinges while all other ridges are removed. **Infinitesimal rigidity conjecture.** All spanning cycles of the $n$-Roberts graph, corresponding to hinged spanning cycles of facets on the $n$-cube, produce an infinitesimally rigid structure: there is no non-trivial first-order deformation that restricts to an infinitesimal congruence on each facet. This conjecture concerns the rigidity of prefabricated hypercube structures formed by hinging facets along the edges of a spanning cycle; establishing it would explain why such structures can be transported in a folded state before unfolding after an additional cut.

341685.title: Ding–Li conjecture on 2-designs from ternary linear codes
341685.literal_statement:
Let $m\ge 3$ be an odd integer, let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$, and let $\mathcal C_1$ and $\mathcal C_2$ be the ternary linear codes defined by

$$
\mathcal{C}_1=\left\\{ \left( \operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}\left( a \alpha^{4i}+b \alpha^{2i} \right) \right)_{i=0}^{\frac{3^m-1}{2}-1}:a,b\in \operatorname{GF}(3^m)\right\\},
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{C}_2=\left\\{ \left( \operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}\left( a \alpha^{\left(3^{\frac{m-3}{2}}+1\right)i}+b \alpha^{\left(3^{\frac{m-1}{2}}+1\right)i} \right) \right)_{i=0}^{\frac{3^m-1}{2}-1}:a,b\in \operatorname{GF}(3^m)\right\\},
$$

where $\operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}$ is the trace from $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$ to $\operatorname{GF}(3)$. For $i\in\\{1,2\\}$, write $A_k(\mathcal C_i)$ for the number of codewords of weight $k$, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i)$ and $\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i)$ denote the point set and the supports of the weight-$k$ codewords, respectively. **Ding–Li's 2-design conjecture.** If $k$ is an integer satisfying $A_k(\mathcal C_i)>1$, then

$$
(\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i),\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i))
$$

is a $2$-design. This is one of the conjectured infinite families of $2$-designs arising from linear projective ternary codes; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

341857.title: The mod-9 q-series conjectures
341857.literal_statement:
For $q$ a formal variable and $(a_1,\ldots,a_r;q^9)_\infty=\prod_{m\geq0}\prod_{j=1}^r(1-a_jq^{9m})$, the five partition conjectures are equivalently expressed by the following $q$-series identities. **Mod-9 q-series conjectures.**

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q,q^3,q^6,q^9;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+3n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^6,q^7;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+2n_1+3n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^3,q^4,q^5,q^6;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+2n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^5,q^8;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{\substack{n_1\geq0\
_2\geq1}}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+4n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}+\sum_{\substack{n_1\geq0\
_2\geq1}}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+2n_1+4n_2+1}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}+\sum_{n_1\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}}=\frac{1}{(q^1,q^4,q^6,q^7;q^9)_\infty}.
$$

These identities remain unproved, although analytic sum-sides for the partition families have been found.

342160.title: The ternary tenth-power block-size conjecture
342160.literal_statement:
Let $m\geq 3$ be odd, and define $k_m$ recursively by

$$
k_m=\frac{3^m+1}{2}+3^{m-1}-3k_{m-2},\qquad k_1=2.
$$
 For $b,c\in {\mathrm{GF}}(3^m)$, let $B_{(x^{10},b,c)}$ denote the corresponding block, and let ${\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},k)}$ be the collection of distinct blocks of size $k$. **The ternary tenth-power block-size conjecture.** The block sizes and multiplicities are

$$
|B_{(x^{10},b,c)}|=\begin{cases}\frac{3^m+1}{2}&\text{for }3^m\text{ choices of }(b,c),\\k_m&\text{for }(3^m-1)3^m\text{ choices of }(b,c),\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
|{\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},(3^m+1)/2)}|=3^m,\qquad |{\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},k_m)}|=\frac{3^m(3^m-1)}{2}.
$$
 Further, the first incidence structure is a symmetric $2$-$(3^m,(3^m+1)/2,(3^m+1)/4)$ design arising from the squares in ${\mathrm{GF}}(3^m)$, and the second is a $2$-$(3^m,k_m,k_m(k_m-1)/2)$ design. This is described as a fundamental open problem concerning designs supported by monomials over odd-characteristic finite fields.

342162.title: The extended designs from Payne, Cherowitzo and Subiaco o-polynomials
342162.literal_statement:
Let $m\geq 5$ be odd, set $q=2^m$, and let $\hat{\mathbb{D}}(f,k)=({\mathrm{GF}}(q),\hat{\mathcal{B}}_k)$ be the extended construction, with $k=q/2$. Define the listed o-polynomials by

$$
\operatorname{Payne}(x)=x^{5/6}+x^{3/6}+x^{1/6},
$$

$$
\operatorname{Cherowitzo}(x)=x^{2^e}+x^{2^e+2}+x^{3\cdot 2^e+4},\qquad e=(m+1)/2,
$$

with its reciprocal variant

$$
\overline{\operatorname{Cherowitzo}}(x)=x^{q-2^e}+x^{q-2^e-2}+x^{q-3\cdot 2^e-4},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Subiaco}_1(x)=(x+x^2+x^3+x^4)(x^4+x^2+1)^{q-2}+x^{2^{m-1}}.
$$
 **The extended special-o-polynomial design conjecture.** For any of these four choices of $f$, $\hat{\mathbb{D}}(f,q/2)$ is a $3$-$(q,q/2,(q-4)(q-1)q/8)$ design. The claim gives explicit further examples of $3$-designs from the extended construction beyond the already covered o-monomial cases. It is stated without a supplied resolution status, so it remains open in this record.

342557.title: Conjecture on cocyclic Hadamard matrices of order 4p
342557.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $W,X,Y,Z$ be circulant blocks defining cocyclic Hadamard matrices of order $4p$. Write $\tau$ for the relevant nontrivial action and $\iota$ for the inversion action. **The cocyclic Hadamard matrix conjecture.** There are no cocyclic Hadamard matrices of the forms

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} W & -X & -Y & -Z\\ X & -W & -Z & -Y\\ Y & -Z & -W & -X\\ Z & -Y & -X & -W \end{array}\right]
$$

and

$$
\left[\begin{array}{llll} W & -X & -Y & -Z\\ X & -W & -Z & -Y\\ Y^{\mathsf T} & -Z^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T}\\ Z^{\mathsf T} & -Y^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} \end{array}\right].
$$

For $p\equiv 1\pmod 4$, there exist cocyclic Hadamard matrices of the form

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} W & X & Y & Z\\ X^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & Z^{\mathsf T} & -Y^{\mathsf T}\\ Y^{\mathsf T} & Z^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T}\\ Z & -Y & -X & W \end{array}\right],
$$

with circulant blocks $W,X,Y,Z$, and these matrices are not equivalent to a Williamson-type matrix or a (transposed) Goethals–Seidel matrix, yielding a new family of cocyclic Hadamard matrices. The first nonexistence assertions correspond respectively to the actions $(\tau,\tau)$ and $(\tau,\iota)$, while the existence assertion corresponds to $(\iota,\iota)$ in the $L_{1,1,0}$ construction.

343321.title: Frankl's conjecture of order $k|\ell$
343321.literal_statement:
Let $\mathfrak{A}_{k|\ell}$ be the class of union-closed families used in the paper, and let $\mathfrak{c}_{k|\ell}$ denote the corresponding supremal proportion of members meeting a $k$-element subset in at least $\ell$ elements. **Frankl's conjecture of order $k|\ell$.** If $\mathcal{A}\in\mathfrak{A}_{k|\ell}$, then there exists $S\subseteq\bigcup\mathcal{A}$ with $|S|=k$ such that at least

$$
2^{-k}\sum_{i=\ell}^k\binom{k}{i}
$$

of the members $A\in\mathcal{A}$ satisfy $|A\cap S|\geq\ell$; equivalently,

$$
\mathfrak{c}_{k|\ell}=2^{-k}\sum_{i=\ell}^k\binom{k}{i}.
$$

In particular, $\mathfrak{c}_{k|1}=2^{-k}(2^k-1)$, $\mathfrak{c}_{k|k}=2^{-k}$, and $\mathfrak{c}_{2k+1|k+1}=2^{-1}$. These variants refine the original Frankl conjecture by prescribing the size and intersection threshold of the witnessing subset; their general validity is open.

343466.title: Kogan's five-type classification conjecture for triples of triangles
343466.literal_statement:
A **linking of triangles** is a set of pairwise disjoint, non-degenerate triangles in 3-space; triangles are understood as their outlines, with unnumbered vertices and no orientation. Two linkings are **combinatorially isotopic** if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of elementary moves, where an elementary move replaces one triangle $ABC$ by $ABC'$ while the swept triangular regions remain disjoint from every other triangle.

**Kogan's classification conjecture.** Any linking of three non-ordered triangles is combinatorially isotopic to one of the following five types: three triangles whose convex hulls are pairwise disjoint; the Borromean or Valknut linking; a Hopf linking of two triangles together with a third triangle whose convex hull is disjoint from the first two; a triangle together with two triangles whose convex hulls are disjoint and both intersect the first triangle at exactly one point; or the specified linking formed by an equilateral triangle and two successive rotations by $\pi/3$ and translations by $\vec h$, where $3\vec h$ is the altitude of the preceding triangle. Linkings from different types should not be combinatorially isotopic.

This conjecture proposes a complete classification of three-triangle linkings under combinatorial isotopy. The paper proves that the standard triple and the Borromean triple are not combinatorially isotopic, but the proposed completeness of the five-type list remains open.

343827.title: The inertia–bicoloring conjecture for full-rank typical graphs
343827.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a full-rank typical graph. A **$G$-partial matrix** is a partial symmetric matrix whose specified off-diagonal entries correspond to the edges of $G$; it is **minimally completable to full rank** if it has a completion of full rank but no proper submatrix obtained by deleting a specified entry has this property. Write $G^c$ for the complement of $G$, and let $\operatorname{In}(M)=(m,n,0)$ denote the common inertia of all completions of $M$, with $m$ positive and $n$ negative eigenvalues. A **proper bicoloring** of $G^c$ assigns red or blue to every vertex so that adjacent vertices have different colors. **Inertia–bicoloring conjecture.** There exists a $G$-partial matrix $M$, minimally completable to full rank, with $\operatorname{In}(M)=(m,n,0)$ if and only if $G^c$ has a proper bicoloring with $m$ red vertices and $n$ blue vertices. The conjecture characterizes the possible inertias of minimally full-rank-completable partial matrices in terms of proper two-colorings of the complement. The stated evidence is that the authors found no full-rank typical graph and corresponding partial matrix whose inertia failed to arise from such a coloring; the general characterization remains open.

343898.title: Interval decomposition conjecture for the nesting-poset zigzag module
343898.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset, and let $\field P$ denote its incidence algebra. For the critical and regular levels $a_0,t_1,a_1,t_2,\dots,t_n,a_n$ associated with the Morse function $f$, let $\field N_{a_i}$ and $\field N_{t_i}$ be the corresponding incidence algebras of nesting posets. **Interval decomposition conjecture.** There is a zigzag module of $\field$-algebras

$$
\field N_{a_0}\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_1}\leftrightarrow\field N_{a_1}\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_2}\leftrightarrow\cdots\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_n}\leftrightarrow\field N_{a_n},
$$

with arrow direction given by Corollary 1, that decomposes into a sum of interval indecomposables of the form

$$
\field_I(t)=\begin{cases}\field\{*\}&\text{if }t\in I\\0&\text{if }t\notin I.\end{cases}
$$

Furthermore, this collection of interval indecomposables determines $f$ up to poset equivalence. This is presented as a structural persistence claim for the nesting posets; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution, so it remains open.

338396.title: The additive-complexity regularity conjecture for automatic sequences
338396.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $\mathbf{w}=w_0w_1w_2\cdots$ be a $k$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $k$-kernel

$$
\{(w_{k^e n+c})_{n\geq 0}\mid e\geq 0,\ 0\leq c<k^e\}
$$

is finite. For each $n\geq 1$, let $\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n)$ denote the number of distinct digit sums of the length-$n$ factors occurring in $\mathbf{w}$. A sequence is **$k$-regular** if the $\mathbb{Z}$-module generated by its $k$-kernel is finitely generated.

**Additive-complexity regularity conjecture.** The sequence $(\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n))_{n\geq 1}$ is $k$-regular.

The conjecture proposes that additive complexity preserves the regularity structure associated with automatic sequences. The paper establishes this property for the specific Thue–Morse-like sequence generated by $0\mapsto01$, $1\mapsto12$, and $2\mapsto20$, but no resolution of the general assertion is provided in the source.

338443.title: Marušič–Scapellato–Zagaglia Salvi compatibility conjecture
338443.literal_statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph. Its canonical double cover has adjacency matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A&0\end{pmatrix}$ when $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $\Gamma$. A graph is **vertex-determining** when distinct vertices have distinct neighborhoods. **Marušič–Scapellato–Zagaglia Salvi's compatibility conjecture.** A connected non-bipartite vertex-determining graph is unstable if and only if it has a compatible adjacency matrix. The source notes that every nontrivially unstable graph has a compatible adjacency matrix, while the conjecture asserts the converse for connected non-bipartite vertex-determining graphs. The paper's preceding theorem establishes that no arc-transitive nontrivially unstable circulant exists, but does not state a resolution of this broader conjecture.

339058.title: Fuller–Gould conjecture on dense $K_4^-$-saturated graphs
339058.literal_statement:
Let $K_4^-$ be the graph obtained from the complete graph $K_4$ by deleting one edge. A graph is **$K_4^-$-saturated** if it contains no copy of $K_4^-$, but adding any missing edge creates at least one copy of $K_4^-$. Write $[a,b]=\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}$.

**Fuller–Gould conjecture.** The $K_4^-$-saturated graphs with sizes in the interval

$$
\left[\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-n+7,\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil\right]
$$

are of two types: complete bipartite graphs with partite sets of nearly equal size, and 3-partite graphs with two partite sets of nearly equal size and one partite set of order one.

This conjecture describes the structure of $K_4^-$-saturated graphs whose numbers of edges are close to the extremal value $\left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor\left\lceil n/2\right\rceil$. The cited work establishes the preceding range of edge sizes up to one below the interval's lower endpoint, while the proposed structural classification for this dense range is not resolved in the supplied source.

339228.title: The partition-weight conjecture in dimensions divisible by four
339228.literal_statement:
Let $d\geq4$ with $d\equiv0\pmod4$, and let $\pi=\{\pi_{i_1\ldots i_{d-1}}\}_{i_1,\ldots,i_{d-1}\geq1}$ be a $(d-1)$-partition. Let $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ be the signed fixed-point weight determined by the unique orientation from the orientation uniqueness conjecture, and let $L_\pi$ denote the corresponding line-bundle factor. **Partition-weight conjecture.** After specializing $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{d-1}=\lambda_d=0$,

$$
L_\pi(0,0,\ldots,-\ell)\,\mathsf{w}_\pi=(-1)^{|\pi|}\omega_\pi\prod_{m=1}^{\pi_{1\cdots1}}(\ell-(m-1)),
$$

for some $\omega_\pi\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, and this positive rational coefficient equals the combinatorial weight $\omega^c_\pi$ defined by decompositions of $\pi$ into binary representations of nonempty $(d-2)$-partitions. The conjecture gives a combinatorial interpretation of the fixed-point contributions and is supported by the calculations described in the paper.

full_record.title: The partition-weight conjecture in dimensions divisible by four
full_record.statement:
Let $d\geq4$ with $d\equiv0\pmod4$, and let $\pi=\{\pi_{i_1\ldots i_{d-1}}\}_{i_1,\ldots,i_{d-1}\geq1}$ be a $(d-1)$-partition. Let $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ be the signed fixed-point weight determined by the unique orientation from the orientation uniqueness conjecture, and let $L_\pi$ denote the corresponding line-bundle factor. **Partition-weight conjecture.** After specializing $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{d-1}=\lambda_d=0$,

$$
L_\pi(0,0,\ldots,-\ell)\,\mathsf{w}_\pi=(-1)^{|\pi|}\omega_\pi\prod_{m=1}^{\pi_{1\cdots1}}(\ell-(m-1)),
$$

for some $\omega_\pi\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, and this positive rational coefficient equals the combinatorial weight $\omega^c_\pi$ defined by decompositions of $\pi$ into binary representations of nonempty $(d-2)$-partitions. The conjecture gives a combinatorial interpretation of the fixed-point contributions and is supported by the calculations described in the paper.
full_record.source_name: Yalong Cao and Martijn Kool, “Counting zero-dimensional subschemes in higher dimensions”, arXiv:1805.04746 (2018).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04746

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

339228.reason_and_missing_lemma: All dimensions divisible by four, fixed-point orientations and positive combinatorial weights required. Orientation uniqueness is itself an explicit dependency; checking partition instances would not prove it. No full localization or weight identity proof; source definitions unread.

339248.title: C$_2$MS model-checking algorithm for graphs of bounded rank-width
339248.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\phi(\mathcal{X})$ be a C$_2$MS formula, and let $\alpha$ be an assignment to its free variables. Write $\operatorname{qr}(\phi)$ for the quantifier rank of $\phi$ and $\operatorname{rwd}(G)$ for the rank-width of $G$. Then there is a computable function $f$ such that the following holds. **C$_2$MS rank-width conjecture.** There exists an algorithm which decides whether

$$
G\models\phi(\alpha(\mathcal{X}))
$$

and whose running time is

$$
\mathcal{O}\bigl(f(\operatorname{qr}(\phi),\operatorname{rwd}(G))\cdot |G|^3\bigr).
$$

This would extend the known fixed-parameter model-checking bounds for monadic second-order logic on graphs of bounded clique-width to the counting extension C$_2$MS and rank-width. The conjecture is presented as an expected algorithmic extension, and its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

339326.title: Extension of the mixed double-dimer construction to all self-intersecting contours
339326.literal_statement:
Let

$$
\{z_{i,j,k}^{(4)}: \left(-k < i,j, i+j < k-1 \mathrm{~for~} k > 0\right) \mathrm{~~and~~} \left( k-1 < i,j, i+j < -k \mathrm{~for~} k \leq 0 \right) \}
$$

be the three-dimensional space of toric cluster variables described in the source. For self-intersecting contours, consider subgraphs with vertices of multiplicity one and two, using mixed configurations in which vertices have multiplicity $1$ except for a simply-connected interior region of vertices of multiplicity $2$. **Extension conjecture.** The construction rule inspired by the family $\varphi\left(A(0,0,n+2)\right)=z_{0,0,n+1}^{(4)}$ extends to all other self-intersecting contours, with an analogue of the taut condition for crossing the inner double-dimer region, and degenerates to the usual dimer-only rule when the self-intersection disappears, namely when $i$, $j$ or $i+j$ falls outside of $[-k,k-1]$ or $[k-1,k]$. The source gives no evidence of resolution.

325385.title: The logarithmic tail conjecture for Kadanoff sandpile configurations
325385.literal:
Let $D$ be a general parameter and let $N$ be any positive integer. Write $\pi(N)$ for the configuration obtained after $N$ grain additions, and let $\pi(N)_{[n,\infty[}$ denote its restriction to columns at least $n$. The notation $^*$ denotes Kleene closure, and $[0]$ denotes at most one zero.

**Logarithmic tail conjecture.** For a general parameter $D$ and all $N$, there exists a column $n$ in $O(\log N)$ such that

$$
\pi(N)_{[n,\infty[}=(D-1,D-2,\dots,2,1)^*[0](D-1,D-2,\dots,2,1)^*0^\omega.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the proved result for $D=3$, asserting that sufficiently far to the right, every configuration has a periodic tail built from the descending block $(D-1,D-2,\dots,1)$, with at most one exceptional zero, beginning at logarithmic distance from the origin. The paper reports that simulations suggest such a generalization, but leaves the claim open.
325385.derivation_and_gap: A fixed-D wave block is not enough: must control transient prefix by O_D(log N) for all N and ensure at most one zero. Local stabilization argument leaves cumulative avalanche/prefix contraction unproved. N=1/log0 endpoint not credited; full intended asymptotic mechanism unpaid.

325981.title: The typical-partite structure conjecture for sparse strictly 2-balanced edge-color-critical graphs
325981.literal:
Let $H$ be a strictly $2$-balanced, edge-color-critical graph. Write $e(H)$ for its number of edges, $\chi(H)$ for its chromatic number, and

$$
m_2(H)=\frac{e(H)-1}{v(H)-2},
$$

where $v(H)$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Let $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}(H)$ be the family of $H$-free graphs with vertex set of size $n$ and exactly $m$ edges. **Typical-partite structure conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that, whenever

$$
m \geq Cn^{2-1/m_2(H)}(\log n)^{1/(e(H)-1)},
$$

almost all graphs in $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}(H)$ are $(\chi(H)-1)$-partite. This would extend known typical-structure results for unrestricted $H$-free graphs to the sparse fixed-edge setting; its status is open in the supplied source.
325981.derivation_and_gap: For each fixed strictly2balanced edge-colour-critical H, a container bound alone counts H-free graphs but does not show almost all lie in (chi(H)-1)-partite family at the displayed exact edge/log threshold. Entropic domination of every nonpartite defect stratum and uniform m-range unpaid. Park.

326701.title: Erde, Golé nia and Golé nia's generalized knight's tour conjecture
326701.literal:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\gcd(a,b)=1,
$$

with $a$ and $b$ not both odd. An $(a,b)$ knight's tour is a cycle visiting every vertex of the corresponding knight's graph on $[n]^d$ exactly once. **Erde, Golé nia and Golé nia's conjecture.** For sufficiently large even $n$ and $d\geq 2$, there is an $(a,b)$ knight's tour in $[n]^d$.

The conjecture proposes a general existence criterion for generalized knight's tours under the necessary parity and coprimality conditions. The stated question of necessary conditions for existence of an $(a,1)$ knight's tour for even $a$ remains open.
326701.derivation_and_gap: gcd/parity are necessary reachability obstructions but not a Hamilton-cycle construction. Tile-and-splice route needs boundary-compatible tours for all residues of sufficiently large even n and every d>=2, with actual knight move definition. Dimension lifting does not solve the planar base; park.

334536.title: Quantitative forcing conjecture for bipartite graphs
334536.literal: Let $H$ be a fixed bipartite graph of girth $g$, and let $p$ be a fixed constant with $0<p<1$. For each $\epsilon>0$, there is a parameter $\delta=\Omega(\epsilon^g)$ such that any graph $G$ of density $p$ satisfying $\mathcal{P}_{H,p}(\delta)$ also satisfies $\mathcal{P}_{2,p}^*(\epsilon)$. **Quantitative forcing conjecture.** The conclusion holds with a forcing parameter of order at least $\epsilon^g$. This is stated as a stronger quantitative version of the forcing conjecture; the source gives no resolution, so the proposed dependence remains open.
334536.derivation_and_gap: Definitions of hereditary P_H,p and P_2,p* not supplied in literal. The girth exponent needs an all-subset discrepancy-to-H-count quantitative bridge; naive cycle moment estimates for a single H do not pay it. A forest has no finite girth g; no repair credited. Primary definitions and full bridge unpaid.

338806.title: High-girth approximation conjecture for uniquely restricted matching number
338806.literal:
For a graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ denote its matching number and $\nu_{ur}(G)$ its uniquely restricted matching number. For every positive real number $\epsilon$ and every positive integer $\Delta$, consider graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g$. **High-girth approximation conjecture.** There is some positive integer $g=g(\epsilon,\Delta)$ such that

$$
\nu_{ur}(G)\geq (1-\epsilon)\nu(G)
$$

for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g$. The conjecture asserts that, for fixed maximum degree, sufficiently large girth makes the uniquely restricted matching number asymptotically as close as desired to the ordinary matching number; the source gives no resolution, so it remains open.

342889.title: The spectrum conjecture for odd sun systems
342889.literal:
Let $k$-sun systems be decompositions of the complete graph $K_v$ into copies of the graph formed from a $k$-cycle by adjoining one pendant edge at each cycle vertex. The necessary conditions for such a system are

$$
v\geq 2k\qquad\text{and}\qquad v(v-1)\equiv 0 \pmod{4k}.
$$

**Spectrum conjecture.** Let $k\geq 3$ and $v>1$. There exists a $k$-sun system of $K_v$ if and only if

$$
v\geq 2k\qquad\text{and}\qquad v(v-1)\equiv 0 \pmod{4k}.
$$

The existence problem is completely settled for several values of $k$, including $k=3,5$, $k=4,6,8$, $k=10,14$, and powers of two at least $4$; a general result also establishes sufficiency when $v$ is sufficiently large relative to $k$. The conjecture asserts that the displayed necessary conditions are sufficient in every remaining case.
342889.derivation_and_gap: Necessary divisibility counts 2k edges per sun, so 4k divides v(v-1); distinct vertices require v>=2k. These do not construct every admissible design. General cycle-decomposition plus distinct pendant assignment avoiding reused edges remains unpaid, especially v near2k. Park after literal review; no primary body read.

345481.title: Eppstein's integer-power conjecture for planar subgraph counts
345481.literal:
Let $H$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\emptyset)$ denote the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph.

**Eppstein's conjecture.** For every graph $H$, there exists a non-negative integer $k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\emptyset)=\Theta(n^k).
$$

This is a restricted planar version of a question posed by Eppstein about subgraph counts in minor-closed graph families. The paper presents it as an open conjecture, while verifying it for trees and establishing general upper bounds.
345481.derivation_and_gap: Literal everyH includes nonplanarH with zero copies in all planar graphs, hence zero is notTheta(n^k); this is only a missing-planarity/domain correction and primary not read. No credit. Intended planarH integer-exponent theorem remains unpaid; bounded-treewidth or degeneracy count need sharp exponent and lower realization.

349348.title: The Nagy conjecture on stability for saturated graphs
349348.literal:
Let $r\ge 2$ be an integer and let $F$ be a graph with chromatic number $r+1$. An **$F$-saturated graph** is an $F$-free graph to which adding any missing edge creates a copy of $F$. Let $t_r(n)$ denote the number of edges in the Turán graph with $r$ parts.

**Nagy's conjecture.** Every $F$-saturated graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t_r(n)-o(n^{\frac{r+1}{r}})$ edges contains a complete $r$-partite subgraph on $(1-o(1))n$ vertices.

This conjecture generalizes the corresponding stability results for saturated complete graphs and odd cycles. The exponent term cannot be improved in the clique case, and for $r=2$ it cannot be improved for any graph $F$ because every 3-chromatic graph contains an odd cycle. The conjecture is open in the stated generality.
349348.derivation_and_gap: Turán stability alone yields approximate edge-partition structure, not a complete multipartite subgraph on almost all vertices. Saturation must force missing cross-edge defects onto o(n) vertices at the n^((r+1)/r) scale for every fixed F. Neither a defect-cover lemma nor a saturated counterfamily was obtained; park.

356539.title: Yuan's additive-constant conjecture for NIM-H edges
356539.literal:
Let $c$ be a $2$-coloring of the edges of $K_n$, let $E(c,H)$ be the set of edges contained in no monochromatic copy of $H$, and define

$$
f(n,H)=\max_c |E(c,H)|.
$$

Let ${\rm ex}(n,H)$ denote the Turán number of $H$. **Yuan's conjecture.** For any graph $H$ and all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a constant $C=C(H)$ such that

$$
f(n,H)={\rm ex}(n,H)+C.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the excess of the maximum number of NIM-$H$ edges over the Turán number eventually stabilizes at a constant depending only on $H$. It is motivated by Yuan's example showing that equality with the Turán number does not hold for every graph $H$; the supplied source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
356539.derivation_and_gap: General H requires eventual exact stabilization, stronger than bounded excess. Colour one extremal H-free graph red gives the ordinary lower construction when its red edges are NIM, but does not bound blue NIM contributions or show eventual constant. Degenerate edgeless-H endpoints not credited. Full structural classification unpaid.

356838.title: Asymptotic sharpness of the lower bound for edge intersection cycles
356838.literal:
Let $k$-uniform hypergraphs be hypergraphs whose hyperedges all have cardinality $k$. Let $C_n$ denote the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $mu^k_n$ be the minimum number of hyperedges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ with edge intersection hypergraph $EI(\mathcal{H})=C_n$.

**Asymptotic sharpness conjecture.** For any $k ge 3$ there exists an $n_k in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n ge n_k$,

$$
\mu^k_n = \left\lceil \frac{3n}{k} \right\rceil.
$$

The equality would show that the general lower bound is asymptotically sharp for every uniformity $k\ge 3$. The paper establishes the equality for sufficiently large $n$ when $k\in\{3,4,6\}$ and when $k=5$ with $n\equiv 0\pmod 5$, while the conjecture remains open for all $k>6$ and also for $k=5$ when $n\not\equiv 0\pmod 5$.
356838.derivation_and_gap: Sustained incidence-dual and local-section routes in SECOND-ROUTE.md. Actual source lower bound read and proved degree>=3. Balanced closed triple sequence with pair occurrences exactly consecutive, uniform column counts and ceiling excess remains unpaid for all k/residue n. No full candidate.

358042.title: Cranston et al.'s revised planar Turán conjecture for cycles
358042.literal:
Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no copy of $C_k$ as a subgraph. Let $d$ be a constant. **Cranston et al.'s revised conjecture.** There exists a constant $d$ such that for all $k$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we have

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k)\le 3n-6-\frac{dn}{k^{\log_2 3}}.
$$

This revised conjecture was proposed after the earlier conjecture of Ghosh et al. was disproved for $k\ge 11$ by Cranston, Lidický, Liu and Shantanam, and independently by Lan and Song. The paper presents it as a proposed asymptotic upper bound for planar Turán numbers of cycles.
358042.derivation_and_gap: Taking d=0 would make Euler bound trivial; intended positive uniform d is necessary and no zero-constant wording credit. General k requires quantitative short-cycle-free planar deficit of order n/k^(log2 3). Separator recursion without exact k-control does not provide it; park.

360678.title: Doubly layered maximizer conjecture at the principal specialization q = -1
360678.literal:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\Phi_w$ denote the principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial at $q=-1$, and let $\mathcal{DL}_n$ denote the set of doubly layered permutations. Define

$$
\widetilde{u}(n):=\max_{w\in S_n}\Phi_w,\qquad \widetilde{v}(n):=\max_{w\in\mathcal{DL}_n}\Phi_w.
$$

**Doubly layered maximizer conjecture.** For every $n$, all permutations reaching the maximum $\widetilde{u}(n)$ are doubly layered permutations. Thus, there is a limit

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2\widetilde{u}(n)}{n^2}.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding asymptotic formula for the doubly layered maximum $\widetilde{v}(n)$, but the unrestricted maximization and the asserted limit remain open.
360678.derivation_and_gap: Need exact principal q-specialization, sign/absolute-value convention and doubly layered definition before any witness. Comparing layered asymptotic exponents cannot prove that EVERY finite-n unrestricted maximizer lies in DL. Local moves need monotonicity and equality characterization globally; unpaid.

363105.title: The asymptotic extremal-size conjecture for forbidden posets
363105.literal:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{La}(n,P)$ be the maximum size of a $P$-free family of subsets of $[n]$. For positive integers $n$ and $x<n$, write $\binom{[n]}{x}$ for the family of $x$-element subsets of $[n]$. Define $e(P)$ to be the largest integer $\ell$ such that, for all $j$ and $n$, the family

$$
\bigcup_{i=1}^{\ell}\binom{[n]}{i+j}
$$

is $P$-free.

**The asymptotic extremal-size conjecture.** For every poset $P$,

$$
\operatorname{La}(n,P)=e(P)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(1+o(1)).
$$

This conjecture generalizes Sperner's theorem. It is unresolved for the two-dimensional Boolean lattice, but has been disproved for the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice when $d\geq 4$.
363105.derivation_and_gap: Universal forbidden-poset asymptotic requires exact weak versus induced containment definition from primary source. Literal report of Boolean-lattice disproof is not proof and not adopted. Chain/Lubell estimates alone do not recover sharp e(P) for all P. Park at all-poset sharp bound/definitions.

364571.title: Minimum-volume scaling conjecture for random triangulations of the d-sphere
364571.literal:
Let $\mathcal{S}^{(d)}_n$ be the set of $n$-vertex triangulations of the $d$-sphere, let $M(\mathcal{S}^{(d)}_n)$ denote their minimum volume, and let $\mu^{(d)}_n$ be the median of this random variable. **Minimum-volume scaling conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ there is a constant $c_d>0$ such that

$$
\mu^{(d)}_n = c_d n^{1-1/d} + o(n^{1-1/d}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the upper bound proved in the paper gives the correct asymptotic order and leading constant form. It is open even for $d=2$; in that case the available bounds constrain $c_2$ to an explicit interval.
364571.derivation_and_gap: Random volume law and triangulation weighting absent from literal; no silent distribution choice. Matching order upper/lower bounds do not imply existence of leading constant c_d for every d. Need asymptotic regularity/subadditivity with normalization and model paid; park, no primary body.

364989.title: 3-colorability conjecture for string graphs of sufficiently large odd girth
364989.literal: Let $k$ be an integer, and consider the class of string graphs whose odd girth is at least $k$. **String-graph coloring conjecture.** There is an integer $k$ such that the class of string graphs of odd girth at least $k$ is 3-chromatic. While string graphs of large odd girth can contain arbitrarily large bipartite complete graphs and therefore are not $d$-degenerate for any fixed $d$, the source gives no known proof or disproof of this 3-colorability assertion.
364989.derivation_and_gap: Large odd girth permits huge bipartite subgraphs, so bounded degeneracy fails as a proof route. A non3colourable high-odd-girth graph must also have an actual string representation; arbitrary high-girth graph existence does not supply one. No such representation or universal colouring lemma; park.

371758.title: Asymptotic feedback vertex set conjecture for bounded-degree digraphs
371758.literal:
For any integer $k\ge 2$, let $f(k)$ be the supremum of ${\rm fvs}(D)/|V(D)|$ over all orgraphs $D$ with maximum degree at most $k$, where ${\rm fvs}(D)$ denotes the minimum feedback vertex set size. **Asymptotic bounded-degree conjecture.** There exists a constant $\theta>0$ such that for all $k\ge 3$,

$$
f(k)\le 1-\theta\cdot\frac{\log_2 k}{k}.
$$

The paper proves exact values for $f(4)$ and $f(5)$ and notes that the conjectured upper bound would be best possible up to the constant, because tournaments provide matching logarithmic-order lower bounds. The conjecture is presented as an open problem for larger maximum degrees.
371758.derivation_and_gap: Earlier same-source371759 is f(6)=4/7, not this allk logarithmic fraction. Literal references a refutation but might refer to a different digirth conjecture: not authenticated. Random ordering only guarantees an independent/acyclic set of order n/(k+1), missing logk. Tournament Ramsey estimates do not bound arbitrary oriented graphs. Full selection lemma unpaid.

372226.title: Draganić–Keevash–Müyesser conjecture on induced $K_r$-factors
372226.literal: Let $r\geq 2$, and let $G$ be an $((r-1)n+1)$-regular graph on $rn$ vertices. A subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ is said to induce a $K_r$-factor when $G[S]$ contains a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$ covering all vertices of $G[S]$. **Draganić–Keevash–Müyesser conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that at least $c2^{rn}$ subsets of $V(G)$ induce a $K_r$-factor. The conjecture is resolved by the result stated in the paper for sufficiently large $n$, while the abstract says that this confirms the conjecture for large $n$.
372226.derivation_and_gap: Literal itself reports a source solution for large n. Earlier same-source372225 concerns Hamiltonian subsets, a distinct scope; do not transfer its disposition. Exact clique-factor theorem/proof and r-dependence of constant c unread. Primary-public-proof HOLD, not authenticated exclusion.

375377.title: The exact asymptotic bound conjecture for small q-kernels
375377.literal:
For integers $q\geq 2$ and $\delta\geq 1$, let $c_{\delta,q}$ be the smallest constant such that every finite digraph $D$ with minimum in-degree at least $\delta$ contains a $q$-kernel of size at most $c_{\delta,q}|V(D)|$. A **$q$-kernel** is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most $q$.

**Exact asymptotic bound conjecture.** For all $\delta\geq 1$ and $q\geq 3$,

$$
c_{\delta,q}=\frac{1}{\delta+1}.
$$

The paper establishes the lower bound $1/(\delta+1)\leq c_{\delta,q}$ and an upper bound of $1/(\lfloor\sqrt{\delta+1}\rfloor+1)$ for $q\geq 3$, while equality is proved when $q\geq \lceil 3\delta/2\rceil+1$. The conjecture remains unresolved in the remaining parameter ranges.
375377.derivation_and_gap: Literal independent q-kernel must dominate outward and minimum degree is inward. A minimum out-degree kernel theorem cannot be silently reversed. Maximal independent set does not guarantee outward radius3 domination with sharp1/(delta+1) cardinality for arbitrarydelta. Full sharp exchange/charging lemma unpaid.

375756.title: Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang asymptotic conjecture for $h_t(\Delta)$
375756.literal:
For positive integers $\Delta$ and $t$, let $h_t(\Delta)$ be the smallest integer such that every graph $G$ with at least $h_t(\Delta)$ edges and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le \Delta$ contains two edges at distance at least $t$. **Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang conjecture.** For $t\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
h_t(\Delta)\le (1+\varepsilon)\Delta^t
$$

for all sufficiently large $\Delta$. This is an asymptotic strengthening of the known general upper bound of order $\frac32\Delta^t$. It remains open according to the supplied paper context.
375756.derivation_and_gap: Earlier same-source375755 refutation is a fixed Delta4 h3 claim, not all sufficiently largeDelta asymptotic bound.375753 and375754 are t2 strong-clique/Ore-degree scopes. No transfer. General BFS edge ball gives wrong leading factor or exponent, not1+epsilon for all fixedt>=3. Primary target/proof unread; park.

376155.title: Liu and Ning's interpolation conjecture for 2-connected subgraphs
376155.literal:
For a fixed integer $q\ge 3$, let $n_0(q)$ be an integer threshold. Let $G$ be a **2-connected graph** of order $n\ge n_0(q)$, and write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree. **Liu and Ning's conjecture.** Every such graph satisfying

$$
\delta(G)\ge \frac{n}{q}
$$

contains a $2$-connected subgraph of order $\ell$ for every $\ell\in\{4,5,\ldots,n\}$. 325385.title: The logarithmic tail conjecture for Kadanoff sandpile configurations
325385.literal:
Let $D$ be a general parameter and let $N$ be any positive integer. Write $\pi(N)$ for the configuration obtained after $N$ grain additions, and let $\pi(N)_{[n,\infty[}$ denote its restriction to columns at least $n$. The notation $^*$ denotes Kleene closure, and $[0]$ denotes at most one zero.

**Logarithmic tail conjecture.** For a general parameter $D$ and all $N$, there exists a column $n$ in $O(\log N)$ such that

$$
\pi(N)_{[n,\infty[}=(D-1,D-2,\dots,2,1)^*[0](D-1,D-2,\dots,2,1)^*0^\omega.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the proved result for $D=3$, asserting that sufficiently far to the right, every configuration has a periodic tail built from the descending block $(D-1,D-2,\dots,1)$, with at most one exceptional zero, beginning at logarithmic distance from the origin. The paper reports that simulations suggest such a generalization, but leaves the claim open.
325385.derivation_and_gap: A fixed-D wave block is not enough: must control transient prefix by O_D(log N) for all N and ensure at most one zero. Local stabilization argument leaves cumulative avalanche/prefix contraction unproved. N=1/log0 endpoint not credited; full intended asymptotic mechanism unpaid.

325981.title: The typical-partite structure conjecture for sparse strictly 2-balanced edge-color-critical graphs
325981.literal:
Let $H$ be a strictly $2$-balanced, edge-color-critical graph. Write $e(H)$ for its number of edges, $\chi(H)$ for its chromatic number, and

$$
m_2(H)=\frac{e(H)-1}{v(H)-2},
$$

where $v(H)$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Let $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}(H)$ be the family of $H$-free graphs with vertex set of size $n$ and exactly $m$ edges. **Typical-partite structure conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that, whenever

$$
m \geq Cn^{2-1/m_2(H)}(\log n)^{1/(e(H)-1)},
$$

almost all graphs in $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}(H)$ are $(\chi(H)-1)$-partite. This would extend known typical-structure results for unrestricted $H$-free graphs to the sparse fixed-edge setting; its status is open in the supplied source.
325981.derivation_and_gap: For each fixed strictly2balanced edge-colour-critical H, a container bound alone counts H-free graphs but does not show almost all lie in (chi(H)-1)-partite family at the displayed exact edge/log threshold. Entropic domination of every nonpartite defect stratum and uniform m-range unpaid. Park.

326701.title: Erde, Golé nia and Golé nia's generalized knight's tour conjecture
326701.literal:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\gcd(a,b)=1,
$$

with $a$ and $b$ not both odd. An $(a,b)$ knight's tour is a cycle visiting every vertex of the corresponding knight's graph on $[n]^d$ exactly once. **Erde, Golé nia and Golé nia's conjecture.** For sufficiently large even $n$ and $d\geq 2$, there is an $(a,b)$ knight's tour in $[n]^d$.

The conjecture proposes a general existence criterion for generalized knight's tours under the necessary parity and coprimality conditions. The stated question of necessary conditions for existence of an $(a,1)$ knight's tour for even $a$ remains open.
326701.derivation_and_gap: gcd/parity are necessary reachability obstructions but not a Hamilton-cycle construction. Tile-and-splice route needs boundary-compatible tours for all residues of sufficiently large even n and every d>=2, with actual knight move definition. Dimension lifting does not solve the planar base; park.

334536.title: Quantitative forcing conjecture for bipartite graphs
334536.literal: Let $H$ be a fixed bipartite graph of girth $g$, and let $p$ be a fixed constant with $0<p<1$. For each $\epsilon>0$, there is a parameter $\delta=\Omega(\epsilon^g)$ such that any graph $G$ of density $p$ satisfying $\mathcal{P}_{H,p}(\delta)$ also satisfies $\mathcal{P}_{2,p}^*(\epsilon)$. **Quantitative forcing conjecture.** The conclusion holds with a forcing parameter of order at least $\epsilon^g$. This is stated as a stronger quantitative version of the forcing conjecture; the source gives no resolution, so the proposed dependence remains open.
334536.derivation_and_gap: Definitions of hereditary P_H,p and P_2,p* not supplied in literal. The girth exponent needs an all-subset discrepancy-to-H-count quantitative bridge; naive cycle moment estimates for a single H do not pay it. A forest has no finite girth g; no repair credited. Primary definitions and full bridge unpaid.

338806.title: High-girth approximation conjecture for uniquely restricted matching number
338806.literal:
For a graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ denote its matching number and $\nu_{ur}(G)$ its uniquely restricted matching number. For every positive real number $\epsilon$ and every positive integer $\Delta$, consider graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g$. **High-girth approximation conjecture.** There is some positive integer $g=g(\epsilon,\Delta)$ such that

$$
\nu_{ur}(G)\geq (1-\epsilon)\nu(G)
$$

for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g$. The conjecture asserts that, for fixed maximum degree, sufficiently large girth makes the uniquely restricted matching number asymptotically as close as desired to the ordinary matching number; the source gives no resolution, so it remains open.

342889.title: The spectrum conjecture for odd sun systems
342889.literal:
Let $k$-sun systems be decompositions of the complete graph $K_v$ into copies of the graph formed from a $k$-cycle by adjoining one pendant edge at each cycle vertex. The necessary conditions for such a system are

$$
v\geq 2k\qquad\text{and}\qquad v(v-1)\equiv 0 \pmod{4k}.
$$

**Spectrum conjecture.** Let $k\geq 3$ and $v>1$. There exists a $k$-sun system of $K_v$ if and only if

$$
v\geq 2k\qquad\text{and}\qquad v(v-1)\equiv 0 \pmod{4k}.
$$

The existence problem is completely settled for several values of $k$, including $k=3,5$, $k=4,6,8$, $k=10,14$, and powers of two at least $4$; a general result also establishes sufficiency when $v$ is sufficiently large relative to $k$. The conjecture asserts that the displayed necessary conditions are sufficient in every remaining case.
342889.derivation_and_gap: Necessary divisibility counts 2k edges per sun, so 4k divides v(v-1); distinct vertices require v>=2k. These do not construct every admissible design. General cycle-decomposition plus distinct pendant assignment avoiding reused edges remains unpaid, especially v near2k. Park after literal review; no primary body read.

345481.title: Eppstein's integer-power conjecture for planar subgraph counts
345481.literal:
Let $H$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\emptyset)$ denote the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph.

**Eppstein's conjecture.** For every graph $H$, there exists a non-negative integer $k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\emptyset)=\Theta(n^k).
$$

This is a restricted planar version of a question posed by Eppstein about subgraph counts in minor-closed graph families. The paper presents it as an open conjecture, while verifying it for trees and establishing general upper bounds.
345481.derivation_and_gap: Literal everyH includes nonplanarH with zero copies in all planar graphs, hence zero is notTheta(n^k); this is only a missing-planarity/domain correction and primary not read. No credit. Intended planarH integer-exponent theorem remains unpaid; bounded-treewidth or degeneracy count need sharp exponent and lower realization.

349348.title: The Nagy conjecture on stability for saturated graphs
349348.literal:
Let $r\ge 2$ be an integer and let $F$ be a graph with chromatic number $r+1$. An **$F$-saturated graph** is an $F$-free graph to which adding any missing edge creates a copy of $F$. Let $t_r(n)$ denote the number of edges in the Turán graph with $r$ parts.

**Nagy's conjecture.** Every $F$-saturated graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t_r(n)-o(n^{\frac{r+1}{r}})$ edges contains a complete $r$-partite subgraph on $(1-o(1))n$ vertices.

This conjecture generalizes the corresponding stability results for saturated complete graphs and odd cycles. The exponent term cannot be improved in the clique case, and for $r=2$ it cannot be improved for any graph $F$ because every 3-chromatic graph contains an odd cycle. The conjecture is open in the stated generality.
349348.derivation_and_gap: Turán stability alone yields approximate edge-partition structure, not a complete multipartite subgraph on almost all vertices. Saturation must force missing cross-edge defects onto o(n) vertices at the n^((r+1)/r) scale for every fixed F. Neither a defect-cover lemma nor a saturated counterfamily was obtained; park.

356539.title: Yuan's additive-constant conjecture for NIM-H edges
356539.literal:
Let $c$ be a $2$-coloring of the edges of $K_n$, let $E(c,H)$ be the set of edges contained in no monochromatic copy of $H$, and define

$$
f(n,H)=\max_c |E(c,H)|.
$$

Let ${\rm ex}(n,H)$ denote the Turán number of $H$. **Yuan's conjecture.** For any graph $H$ and all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a constant $C=C(H)$ such that

$$
f(n,H)={\rm ex}(n,H)+C.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the excess of the maximum number of NIM-$H$ edges over the Turán number eventually stabilizes at a constant depending only on $H$. It is motivated by Yuan's example showing that equality with the Turán number does not hold for every graph $H$; the supplied source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
356539.derivation_and_gap: General H requires eventual exact stabilization, stronger than bounded excess. Colour one extremal H-free graph red gives the ordinary lower construction when its red edges are NIM, but does not bound blue NIM contributions or show eventual constant. Degenerate edgeless-H endpoints not credited. Full structural classification unpaid.

356838.title: Asymptotic sharpness of the lower bound for edge intersection cycles
356838.literal:
Let $k$-uniform hypergraphs be hypergraphs whose hyperedges all have cardinality $k$. Let $C_n$ denote the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $mu^k_n$ be the minimum number of hyperedges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ with edge intersection hypergraph $EI(\mathcal{H})=C_n$.

**Asymptotic sharpness conjecture.** For any $k ge 3$ there exists an $n_k in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n ge n_k$,

$$
\mu^k_n = \left\lceil \frac{3n}{k} \right\rceil.
$$

The equality would show that the general lower bound is asymptotically sharp for every uniformity $k\ge 3$. The paper establishes the equality for sufficiently large $n$ when $k\in\{3,4,6\}$ and when $k=5$ with $n\equiv 0\pmod 5$, while the conjecture remains open for all $k>6$ and also for $k=5$ when $n\not\equiv 0\pmod 5$.
356838.derivation_and_gap: Sustained incidence-dual and local-section routes in SECOND-ROUTE.md. Actual source lower bound read and proved degree>=3. Balanced closed triple sequence with pair occurrences exactly consecutive, uniform column counts and ceiling excess remains unpaid for all k/residue n. No full candidate.

358042.title: Cranston et al.'s revised planar Turán conjecture for cycles
358042.literal:
Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no copy of $C_k$ as a subgraph. Let $d$ be a constant. **Cranston et al.'s revised conjecture.** There exists a constant $d$ such that for all $k$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we have

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k)\le 3n-6-\frac{dn}{k^{\log_2 3}}.
$$

This revised conjecture was proposed after the earlier conjecture of Ghosh et al. was disproved for $k\ge 11$ by Cranston, Lidický, Liu and Shantanam, and independently by Lan and Song. The paper presents it as a proposed asymptotic upper bound for planar Turán numbers of cycles.
358042.derivation_and_gap: Taking d=0 would make Euler bound trivial; intended positive uniform d is necessary and no zero-constant wording credit. General k requires quantitative short-cycle-free planar deficit of order n/k^(log2 3). Separator recursion without exact k-control does not provide it; park.

360678.title: Doubly layered maximizer conjecture at the principal specialization q = -1
360678.literal:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\Phi_w$ denote the principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial at $q=-1$, and let $\mathcal{DL}_n$ denote the set of doubly layered permutations. Define

$$
\widetilde{u}(n):=\max_{w\in S_n}\Phi_w,\qquad \widetilde{v}(n):=\max_{w\in\mathcal{DL}_n}\Phi_w.
$$

**Doubly layered maximizer conjecture.** For every $n$, all permutations reaching the maximum $\widetilde{u}(n)$ are doubly layered permutations. Thus, there is a limit

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2\widetilde{u}(n)}{n^2}.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding asymptotic formula for the doubly layered maximum $\widetilde{v}(n)$, but the unrestricted maximization and the asserted limit remain open.
360678.derivation_and_gap: Need exact principal q-specialization, sign/absolute-value convention and doubly layered definition before any witness. Comparing layered asymptotic exponents cannot prove that EVERY finite-n unrestricted maximizer lies in DL. Local moves need monotonicity and equality characterization globally; unpaid.

363105.title: The asymptotic extremal-size conjecture for forbidden posets
363105.literal:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{La}(n,P)$ be the maximum size of a $P$-free family of subsets of $[n]$. For positive integers $n$ and $x<n$, write $\binom{[n]}{x}$ for the family of $x$-element subsets of $[n]$. Define $e(P)$ to be the largest integer $\ell$ such that, for all $j$ and $n$, the family

$$
\bigcup_{i=1}^{\ell}\binom{[n]}{i+j}
$$

is $P$-free.

**The asymptotic extremal-size conjecture.** For every poset $P$,

$$
\operatorname{La}(n,P)=e(P)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(1+o(1)).
$$

This conjecture generalizes Sperner's theorem. It is unresolved for the two-dimensional Boolean lattice, but has been disproved for the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice when $d\geq 4$.
363105.derivation_and_gap: Universal forbidden-poset asymptotic requires exact weak versus induced containment definition from primary source. Literal report of Boolean-lattice disproof is not proof and not adopted. Chain/Lubell estimates alone do not recover sharp e(P) for all P. Park at all-poset sharp bound/definitions.

364571.title: Minimum-volume scaling conjecture for random triangulations of the d-sphere
364571.literal:
Let $\mathcal{S}^{(d)}_n$ be the set of $n$-vertex triangulations of the $d$-sphere, let $M(\mathcal{S}^{(d)}_n)$ denote their minimum volume, and let $\mu^{(d)}_n$ be the median of this random variable. **Minimum-volume scaling conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ there is a constant $c_d>0$ such that

$$
\mu^{(d)}_n = c_d n^{1-1/d} + o(n^{1-1/d}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the upper bound proved in the paper gives the correct asymptotic order and leading constant form. It is open even for $d=2$; in that case the available bounds constrain $c_2$ to an explicit interval.
364571.derivation_and_gap: Random volume law and triangulation weighting absent from literal; no silent distribution choice. Matching order upper/lower bounds do not imply existence of leading constant c_d for every d. Need asymptotic regularity/subadditivity with normalization and model paid; park, no primary body.

364989.title: 3-colorability conjecture for string graphs of sufficiently large odd girth
364989.literal: Let $k$ be an integer, and consider the class of string graphs whose odd girth is at least $k$. **String-graph coloring conjecture.** There is an integer $k$ such that the class of string graphs of odd girth at least $k$ is 3-chromatic. While string graphs of large odd girth can contain arbitrarily large bipartite complete graphs and therefore are not $d$-degenerate for any fixed $d$, the source gives no known proof or disproof of this 3-colorability assertion.
364989.derivation_and_gap: Large odd girth permits huge bipartite subgraphs, so bounded degeneracy fails as a proof route. A non3colourable high-odd-girth graph must also have an actual string representation; arbitrary high-girth graph existence does not supply one. No such representation or universal colouring lemma; park.

371758.title: Asymptotic feedback vertex set conjecture for bounded-degree digraphs
371758.literal:
For any integer $k\ge 2$, let $f(k)$ be the supremum of ${\rm fvs}(D)/|V(D)|$ over all orgraphs $D$ with maximum degree at most $k$, where ${\rm fvs}(D)$ denotes the minimum feedback vertex set size. **Asymptotic bounded-degree conjecture.** There exists a constant $\theta>0$ such that for all $k\ge 3$,

$$
f(k)\le 1-\theta\cdot\frac{\log_2 k}{k}.
$$

The paper proves exact values for $f(4)$ and $f(5)$ and notes that the conjectured upper bound would be best possible up to the constant, because tournaments provide matching logarithmic-order lower bounds. The conjecture is presented as an open problem for larger maximum degrees.
371758.derivation_and_gap: Earlier same-source371759 is f(6)=4/7, not this allk logarithmic fraction. Literal references a refutation but might refer to a different digirth conjecture: not authenticated. Random ordering only guarantees an independent/acyclic set of order n/(k+1), missing logk. Tournament Ramsey estimates do not bound arbitrary oriented graphs. Full selection lemma unpaid.

372226.title: Draganić–Keevash–Müyesser conjecture on induced $K_r$-factors
372226.literal: Let $r\geq 2$, and let $G$ be an $((r-1)n+1)$-regular graph on $rn$ vertices. A subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ is said to induce a $K_r$-factor when $G[S]$ contains a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$ covering all vertices of $G[S]$. **Draganić–Keevash–Müyesser conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that at least $c2^{rn}$ subsets of $V(G)$ induce a $K_r$-factor. The conjecture is resolved by the result stated in the paper for sufficiently large $n$, while the abstract says that this confirms the conjecture for large $n$.
372226.derivation_and_gap: Literal itself reports a source solution for large n. Earlier same-source372225 concerns Hamiltonian subsets, a distinct scope; do not transfer its disposition. Exact clique-factor theorem/proof and r-dependence of constant c unread. Primary-public-proof HOLD, not authenticated exclusion.

375377.title: The exact asymptotic bound conjecture for small q-kernels
375377.literal:
For integers $q\geq 2$ and $\delta\geq 1$, let $c_{\delta,q}$ be the smallest constant such that every finite digraph $D$ with minimum in-degree at least $\delta$ contains a $q$-kernel of size at most $c_{\delta,q}|V(D)|$. A **$q$-kernel** is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most $q$.

**Exact asymptotic bound conjecture.** For all $\delta\geq 1$ and $q\geq 3$,

$$
c_{\delta,q}=\frac{1}{\delta+1}.
$$

The paper establishes the lower bound $1/(\delta+1)\leq c_{\delta,q}$ and an upper bound of $1/(\lfloor\sqrt{\delta+1}\rfloor+1)$ for $q\geq 3$, while equality is proved when $q\geq \lceil 3\delta/2\rceil+1$. The conjecture remains unresolved in the remaining parameter ranges.
375377.derivation_and_gap: Literal independent q-kernel must dominate outward and minimum degree is inward. A minimum out-degree kernel theorem cannot be silently reversed. Maximal independent set does not guarantee outward radius3 domination with sharp1/(delta+1) cardinality for arbitrarydelta. Full sharp exchange/charging lemma unpaid.

375756.title: Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang asymptotic conjecture for $h_t(\Delta)$
375756.literal:
For positive integers $\Delta$ and $t$, let $h_t(\Delta)$ be the smallest integer such that every graph $G$ with at least $h_t(\Delta)$ edges and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le \Delta$ contains two edges at distance at least $t$. **Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang conjecture.** For $t\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
h_t(\Delta)\le (1+\varepsilon)\Delta^t
$$

for all sufficiently large $\Delta$. This is an asymptotic strengthening of the known general upper bound of order $\frac32\Delta^t$. It remains open according to the supplied paper context.

376155.title: Liu and Ning's interpolation conjecture for 2-connected subgraphs
376155.literal:
For a fixed integer $q\ge 3$, let $n_0(q)$ be an integer threshold. Let $G$ be a **2-connected graph** of order $n\ge n_0(q)$, and write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree. **Liu and Ning's conjecture.** Every such graph satisfying

$$
\delta(G)\ge \frac{n}{q}
$$

contains a $2$-connected subgraph of order $\ell$ for every $\ell\in\{4,5,\ldots,n\}$. This conjecture seeks an asymptotic minimum-degree threshold guaranteeing 2-connected subgraphs of every possible order; the preceding results establish stronger degree thresholds, namely approximately $n/3$ and $n/4$, but the proposed $n/q$ threshold for every fixed $q\ge 3$ remains unresolved.
